What

What Cherry Tree Pruning Involves

Cherry tree pruning is species-specific work built around two realities: bloom timing and disease vulnerability. Flowering ornamental cherries are best pruned immediately after spring flowering ends — roughly late April through mid-May in NE Ohio — because late-winter pruning strips the flower buds that carry next season's display. Fruiting sweet and tart cherries follow a modified open-center training system, best maintained in midsummer when disease pressure is lowest.

The distinction that matters most is disease. Cherries are highly susceptible to bacterial canker (Pseudomonas syringae) and silverleaf disease (Chondrostereum purpureum), both of which enter through fresh wounds in cool, wet conditions. Every Roubic cherry job is timed for dry weather, cut to ANSI A300 standards, and done with tools sterilized between cuts to keep infection risk down.

Common Cherry Pruning Questions

Cherry Tree Pruning FAQ

Five things NE Ohio homeowners want to know before booking.

When should flowering cherries be pruned?
Immediately after flowering ends — late April through mid-May in NE Ohio. Late-winter pruning removes the flower buds that carry next year's bloom, and late-fall cuts in cool, wet weather raise bacterial canker risk. Post-bloom is the safe window.
Why does my cherry tree have oozing, gummy wounds?
That's usually bacterial canker (Pseudomonas syringae), common on stressed cherries. Affected branches should be pruned well below the visible damage, in dry weather, with tools sterilized between cuts. Severely affected trees may need removal — Aaron will tell you honestly during the estimate.
Can I top a cherry tree?
No. Topping is malpractice on any species and especially harmful on cherries because of their disease vulnerability. Where a canopy genuinely needs to shrink, proper crown reduction cut back to healthy laterals is the correct approach.
How much does cherry pruning cost?
Cherry pruning typically runs quoted on-site depending on size and scope. Disease-related remediation pruning can run higher when extensive branch removal is needed — that work is quoted on-site during your free estimate.
Do you prune cherry trees across all of NE Ohio?
Yes. Cherry pruning is available across our full 13-city service area from our Auburn Township yard — Tier 1 cities like Pepper Pike, Chagrin Falls, Moreland Hills, and Solon get priority scheduling, with Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities scheduled soon after. Every estimate is free and on-site.
